text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Thursday it had struck an agreement to buy about 55 percent of Chateau d'Yquem, the producer of one of France's most prestigious regional wines.
LVMH did not disclose the purchase price, but an industry expert put the value of 100 percent of Chateau d'Yquem at around one billion francs.
"Several members of the families associated with the Chateau d'Yquem have concluded an accord with LVMH," the company said in a statement.
"The Marquis de Lur-Saluces has joined the accord and an agreement has been established. Under the terms, LVMH is acquiring around 55 percent of Yquem," it said.

A spokeswoman said the accord applies to 55 percent of the 113-hectare property in southwestern France. She said the prestige of Chateau d'Yquem's Sauternes wines, served with desserts and foie gras, justified the acquisition.
The newspaper Le Figaro said on Thursday that the deal represented LVMH's first purchase of a winemaker. The group's brands include Moet & Chandon champagnes and Hennessy cognacs.
